description: I'm Ranyan, a developer building digital platforms for African markets. Our project, Field Shift Ghana, turns live NASA POWER climate data into a simple three-season crop rotation plan for Ghanaian smallholder farmers, plus a climate check for tree crops like cocoa. The app is already live. We're looking for people with agronomy, data analysis or design skills to help us polish and present it.
summary: Field Shift Ghana is a mobile-first web app that helps Ghanaian smallholder farmers plan their next three seasons as the climate shifts. A farmer picks their region (all 16 regions of Ghana), describes their field (soil, water access, last crop) and chooses a priority. The app reads 24 years (2001 to 2024) of live NASA POWER rainfall and temperature data for that area, shows how the climate is changing per decade, rates dry-spell risk, and recommends a three-season crop rotation with a plain-language reason for every crop. It also rates how well the long-term climate suits tree crops such as cocoa, oil palm, cashew and shea. Plans can be shared on WhatsApp. It answers the challenge by combining NASA Earth observations, field conditions and farmer priorities in one simple decision-support tool.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Field Shift Ghana gives smallholder farmers a clear plan in three taps: where is your farm, what is your field like, and what matters most. It then shows how rainfall and temperature have changed over 24 years in their area, rates dry-spell risk, and recommends a three-season crop rotation with a plain-language reason for each crop. A second card rates long-term climate suitability for tree crops (cocoa, oil palm, cashew, shea). The plan can be shared on WhatsApp.

HOW IT WORKS AND NASA DATA

The app calls the NASA POWER API live from the browser for the farmer's region and reads annual rainfall (PRECTOTCORR) and 2 m air temperature (T2M) for 2001 to 2024. It calculates the trend per decade and a dry-spell risk level. A transparent rule-based engine covering 13 annual crops then builds the rotation: never the same crop family in back-to-back seasons, cereals alternated with legumes, drought-tolerant crops favoured when rainfall is falling, adjusted for soil type, rain-fed or irrigated water access, and the farmer's priority. Tree crops are rated separately because they stay in the ground for decades and cannot be rotated.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

It turns satellite data into advice farmers can act on, to protect soil, save water and reduce risk as rainfall patterns change.

TOOLS

React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, NASA POWER API. Hosted on Vercel.

DESIGN AND FACTORS CONSIDERED

Few choices per screen, tap-to-choose options with no typing, large touch targets, clear system status (a badge shows whether data is live or sample), keyboard and screen-reader support, and plain language. The app labels data honestly if NASA's service cannot be reached.

LIMITATIONS

Decision support only. Rotation rules are simple and based on general agronomy. Tree-crop ratings use climate only, on satellite data averaged over areas about 50 km wide, so local conditions can differ. Farmers should confirm with their local agricultural extension officer or COCOBOD.

AI (SUPER INTELLIGENCE) ACKNOWLEDGEMENT

AI tools helped build this project. The interface was first generated with Bolt.new, then developed, tested and audited with an AI coding agent in Antigravity IDE, and Claude (Anthropic) helped with planning, prompts, rotation-rule design and writing. All code and text produced with AI assistance is acknowledged here, in the README and in the app's page metadata. I reviewed and tested the results.
